history.heading: The Bruneian Empire
paragraphs: Brunei, on the northern coast of the island of Borneo, was an early trading centre linked with China. From the 15th century its rulers adopted Islam, and the Sultanate of Brunei grew into a powerful maritime empire that, at its peak in the 16th century under Sultan Bolkiah, controlled much of Borneo's coast and parts of the southern Philippines.

Brunei declined from the 17th century due to internal conflicts and European expansion. In the 19th century it lost large territories to the British adventurer James Brooke, who became the White Rajah of Sarawak, and to the North Borneo Company.

history.heading: Protectorate and independence
paragraphs: Brunei became a British protectorate in 1888. Oil was discovered at Seria in 1929, transforming the small state's fortunes. During the Second World War it was occupied by Japan.

A revolt in 1962 by those favouring a democratic, united northern Borneo state was suppressed with British help, and the sultan chose not to join the new federation of Malaysia in 1963. Brunei became fully independent on 1 January 1984. Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah has reigned since 1967.

culture.heading: Malay Islamic Monarchy
paragraphs: Brunei's national philosophy is Melayu Islam Beraja (Malay Islamic Monarchy), combining Malay culture, Islam and loyalty to the sultan. Malay is the official language, and English is widely used. Most people are Muslim; there are also Chinese and indigenous communities.
Landmarks include the Omar Ali Saifuddien Mosque and Kampong Ayer, a large water village built on stilts. The national dish is ambuyat, a starchy sago dish eaten with sauces.

politics.heading: Absolute monarchy
paragraphs: Brunei is an absolute monarchy. The sultan is head of state and also prime minister and holds other ministerial posts. There have been no elections for parliament since 1962, and the Legislative Council is appointed.
In 2014 Brunei began implementing a Sharia penal code, which drew international criticism, especially over severe penalties. Brunei is a member of ASEAN and the Commonwealth.

economy.heading: Oil and gas wealth
paragraphs: Oil and natural gas account for the majority of exports and government revenue, giving Brunei a high standard of living. Citizens pay no personal income tax and receive free education and healthcare.
The government is trying to diversify, with petrochemical and refining projects, fisheries and tourism, as hydrocarbon reserves decline. The Brunei dollar is pegged to the Singapore dollar.
